- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent dip (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), true price often reverses or lags — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or mildly positive), model overestimates mean — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (avg > 0.2), model often over-optimistically forecasts upward — reduce forecast by 3–7% for 10+ day horizon.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by 2–5% over 3–5 day horizon, apply “lag correction” — subtract 0.5–1.5% per day for remaining days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for noise and mean reversion bias.
